incidents.vector: AI-assisted phishing-kit subscription service (from $88/week) generated fake brand sites to harvest card and account credentials, traced to 3.9 million stolen cards.
incidents.impact: FBI, Google and Lumen dismantled the operation ('Operation Ghost Hook'), seizing admin servers, domains and wallets after an estimated $1.9 billion in global losses.

incidents.vector: Data breach reportedly traced to a Chinese software engineer employed by the company who has since left the country.
incidents.impact: Exposed personal data of 34 million customers; South Korea's PIPC levied a record $409 million fine. Coupang says it will appeal.

incidents.vector: Intrusion at a government agency managing healthcare entitlements; stolen records subsequently surfaced on online black markets.
incidents.impact: Personal information of more than 67 million Thai citizens allegedly stolen; the Thai government has opened an investigation.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the congressman's Signal messaging account; the FBI notified him this week.
incidents.impact: Suspected Russian operators breached the Signal account of a prominent Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic, raising espionage concerns.

incidents.vector: Conti ransomware deployed against networks worldwide; a member developed malware used in the attacks.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty in U.S. federal court; the FBI estimates Conti extorted over $150 million from 1,000+ victims before disbanding in 2022.

incidents.vector: Threat actor contacted the health ministry's National Health Fund demanding payment to prevent release of allegedly stolen data.
incidents.impact: The Jamaican government says it is still investigating whether a breach occurred.
A hacktivist group defaced the official website of the Philippines Senate.

incidents.victim: Higher education sector — 100+ orgs (incl. University of Nottingham)
incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft (CVE-2026-35273, CVSS 9.8 RCE in the Environment Management Hub), then MeshCentral C2, SSH credential spraying and bulk data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters claims 300+ PeopleSoft instances across 100+ organizations (68% higher education); the University of Nottingham confirmed theft of a significant amount of student/alumni data (450,000+ records, 40GB claimed) and victims are being extorted.

incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of CVE-2026-10520 (CVSS 10 OS command injection) via a public proof-of-concept within 24 hours of disclosure, giving unauthenticated root-level remote code execution.
incidents.impact: Shadowserver observed widespread exploitation with vulnerable instances already backdoored; added to CISA's KEV catalog. Compromise exposes stored credentials and directory connections on the mobile gateway.

incidents.vector: Russia-aligned group used stolen session tokens and commercial proxy/VPN infrastructure to access cloud accounts and harvest bulk email and files.
incidents.impact: Russian national Denis Obrezko was charged in U.S. federal court for providing infrastructure to the espionage campaign; the FBI verified intrusions at at least 11 U.S. companies, likely a fraction of the total.

incidents.vector: Cybersecurity incident affecting the school's ICT systems.
incidents.impact: The 1,428-pupil school sent most students home for a second day and remained closed except for exam candidates while working with cybersecurity specialists and the NCSC.

incidents.vector: Social-engineering attempts luring users to malicious links, plus creation of WhatsApp test accounts and groups.
incidents.impact: Meta says it disrupted the campaign and is asking a court to hold NSO in contempt for violating a 2025 permanent injunction barring it from targeting WhatsApp.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupting operational systems at the start of the sugarcane crushing season.
incidents.impact: Australia's second-largest sugar producer paused cane haulage and milling at two Mackay-region mills, disrupting the harvest.

incidents.vector: Repeated network intrusions by attackers linked to foreign governments, per a former IBM threat-intelligence VP's whistleblower lawsuit.
incidents.impact: The suit alleges both companies concealed multiple breaches from the U.S. government and made false security assurances to win and keep federal contracts.

incidents.victim: Instagram accounts (Obama White House, U.S. Space Force)
incidents.vector: Social engineering of Meta's AI customer-support bot, tricking it into linking attacker emails to target accounts and issuing password-reset codes; accounts with MFA were not affected.
incidents.impact: High-profile Instagram accounts were briefly defaced with pro-Iran messages; Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached.
